conventions.convention: P is a constant-rank C² orthogonal projector on finite-dimensional C^d; the Hermitian inner product is v* w, the projected connection is P d, and Kato transport solves W'=[P',P]W with W(0)=I.
Exterior derivatives at finite regularity are componentwise coordinate derivatives; matrix-valued wedge products use ordered matrix multiplication and alternation.
Boundary orientation is outward-normal-first. Surface regions permit regular C² boundary arcs and finitely many corners with linearly independent incident tangents.
The connection form A=V* dV is anti-Hermitian; curvature is dA+A∧A. Under V'=Vg, A'=g⁻¹Ag+g⁻¹dg and curvature transforms by conjugation.

The Chern normalization is (i/2π)∫tr F. Parallel transport contributes exp(−∫A), and a frame change u_next=u_current g contributes g⁻¹. Clutching winding uses the orientation of the northern subsurface boundary.
The sphere has outward orientation and area form ω_n(u,v)=n·(u×v). For P_+=(I+n·σ)/2, tr F=(i/2)ω, the Chern number is −1, and holonomy is exp(−iΩ/2), with Ω defined modulo 4π.
H has energy units joules, ℏ has joule-seconds, T has seconds, and s=t/T is dimensionless. The spectral cluster must be continuously followed and uniformly separated from its complement.
Chern integrality and solid-angle filling independence assume full AC; the finite adiabatic estimate and C¹ Stokes lemma explicitly assume Countable Choice.

load_bearing.statement: For a C² constant-rank orthogonal projector, the projected connection has curvature F=P(dP∧dP)P. In a local C² orthonormal frame, A=V*dV and dA+A∧A=V*FV; frame changes give the stated connection and curvature covariance.
Assume full AC. For a C² rank-one orthogonal projector on a compact boundaryless oriented smooth surface Σ, (i/2π)∫Σ tr F=⟨c₁(E_P),[Σ]⟩∈Z.
Under Countable Choice and the stated compact surface-region, regular C² arc and corner hypotheses, a complex C¹ one-form satisfies ∫D dη=∫∂D η with outward-normal-first boundary orientation.

The range of a C² constant-rank orthogonal projector is a C² complex vector bundle; P d is a Hermitian connection at the specified regularity; along every C² path, the Kato equation has a unique C² unitary solution intertwining the projectors.

Under full AC, the rank-one curvature integral is the integral Chern pairing; closed-path holonomy is the product of exp(−∫A) factors and inverse frame transitions. For the stated two-subsurface decomposition with supplied frames u_S=u_Ng, the Chern number equals wind(g).

Under Countable Choice, a C² finite Hermitian family with a coherently followed uniformly gapped spectral cluster has leakage at most ℏC/T with the displayed commutator-solution constant. For rank one, U_A(s)P(0)=exp(−iT∫₀ˢE/ℏ)W(s)P(0).

concerns.concern: F7 concludes that evaluation on a smooth representative of the real fundamental class equals the oriented manifold integral, and step 2.1 uses this conclusion. The opened comparison suppliers establish smooth-cycle representatives and evaluation as a sum of simplex integrals; they do not explicitly identify that sum with the chart-partition manifold integral for the locally orientation-defined fundamental class. The standard compatibility is true, but this passage needs an exact supplier or a local orientation/integration argument.

alerts.finding: The title says “The determinant-line projector is smooth and rank one,” whereas the Definition assumes only C² P and the Statement and step 4.1 prove only C² Q. For m=1, Q=P. On M=R, take θ(t)=|t|³, u(t)=(cos θ(t),sin θ(t)) and P=uu*. This is a C² rank-one orthogonal projector whose off-diagonal entry is not C³ at zero, so Q need not be smooth. The stronger wording also appears in lem-nrqmx-determinant-curvature-is-trace F2: “proves that Q is a smooth rank-one orthogonal projector.” The actual determinant-curvature calculation only needs C².

The opening paragraph's displayed inline Chern convention contains doubled literal backslashes before pi, int, operatorname and wedge. These are TeX line-break commands rather than the intended single-backslash mathematical commands, so the formula needs a rendering correction.
